Backup and Restore
Export your settings, per-user profiles, and saved color scenes as a credential-safe JSON document. Stored bridge keys are never included; importing on this server preserves matching keys. For a migration, enter replacement keys below; they stay in this page's memory and are sent only with the atomic import request. Use Validate Import to run a non-mutating dependency and configuration preflight before confirming the replacement.
Imports are atomic and are rejected while playback is active.
Migration credentials (optional)
Leave fields blank when importing back to the same server; matching stored keys are preserved automatically. For a new server, enter the replacement App Key and Client Key for each target that needs them. Values are not added to the downloaded file or saved in the browser.
Bridge connection

Global Channel Profile
Choose the entertainment channels driven by the default profile. Leave this field blank to drive every channel. Per-user mappings with a populated channel override take precedence; blank per-user fields inherit this global selection.
Optional comma-separated Hue entertainment channel IDs (0-65535). Load Channel IDs after selecting an area; the stored global App Key is used when the secret field is blank. Edit the list to choose a subset. Test Connection validates this global selection.
Scene Effect Preview
Preview a solid color, breathing Pulse, hue-cycling Rainbow, warm flickering Candle, cycling warm-to-cool Temperature, drifting green-to-violet Aurora, high-energy Fire, rolling blue/cyan Ocean, electric blue/white Lightning, or cool white/blue Starlight effect on the default bridge target—or every distinct enabled target—for a few seconds. Set animation speed from 25% to 400% for non-solid effects. The selected lights are saved and restored automatically. Use Fade in and Fade out for smooth scene boundaries; saved scenes carry the effect, speed, and transitions into scheduled cues. All-target preview uses each target's saved channel profile and runs sequentially, reporting independent outcomes. Capture Current Light Color reads one target or a selected/all-target set, reports each room independently, and seeds this editor with a weighted aggregate RGB/brightness sample, making it easy to save a multi-room snapshot as a reusable scene. Saved Scene Playlists can chain these reusable scenes in a chosen order. Stop active playback before previewing or capturing.
Uses the selected preview target profile above. The default button uses the target selection; Preview All Enabled Targets is an explicit broadcast override. Nested ↳ device rows send only credential-free user/device route identifiers, so an individual mapped device can be previewed without changing bridge credentials or saved mappings. Current-light capture has its own target selector and reports per-target results without changing bridge state.
Select saved scenes to preview sequentially with restorative state cleanup. The Saved Scene Preview Targets selection above applies to bulk previews; the All Targets button is an explicit broadcast override. Duplicate independent copies or delete selected scenes together. Any playlist or scheduled-cue reference blocks deletion.
Save a color, effect, animation speed, brightness, duration, and optional fade-in/fade-out as a reusable scene. Choose the default bridge, all enabled targets, a mapped user, or a nested ↳ device route in Saved Scene Preview Targets; route requests carry only the user and device identifiers. Preview Saved Scene uses that selection; Preview Saved Scene on All Targets is an explicit broadcast override. Use Duplicate Scene to create a safe editable variant, enter a new name and use Rename Scene to migrate playlist and scheduled-cue references atomically, or use View References before changing/deleting a scene. Scenes contain no bridge credentials. A scene cannot be deleted while a playlist or scheduled cue still references it.
Saved Scene Playlists
Compose up to 20 saved scenes into a playlist. Each step inherits its saved scene's RGB color, brightness, effect speed, fade transitions, and fade curve unless you set explicit 0-255 red/green/blue channel values, 0-100% brightness, 25-400% effect speed, 0-30 second fade-in, 0-30 second fade-out, or Linear/SmoothStep/EaseIn/EaseOut/EaseInOut curve overrides; blank fields and Inherited scene curves preserve the saved scene. Its hold duration inherits the scene by default or can use a bounded per-step override from 1-30 seconds (0 means inherit). Choose Saved order or a stable date-seeded Shuffle for each restorative preview pass. Repeat the complete sequence up to 10 times when the bounded total duration remains at or below 10 minutes. Choose the default target, all enabled targets, or a deliberate subset of enabled mappings and optionally include the default bridge. Playlist definitions contain only scene names, per-step duration/RGB/brightness/effect-speed/transition/curve overrides, repeat count, playback order, and credential-free target selection, never bridge credentials. Preview Targets can override one preview run with mapped users or nested ↳ device routes without changing the saved playlist; Preview Playlist on All Targets remains an explicit broadcast override. Renaming a playlist automatically updates scheduled cues that use it; use View References to inspect dependent cues before deletion, which remains blocked until those cues are changed or removed.
Select playlists to preview with their saved order or stable daily shuffle and restorative state cleanup. Preview Selected uses each playlist's saved target unless Bulk preview targets is changed; the All Targets button remains an explicit broadcast override. Duplicate independent copies or delete them together. Any playlist referenced by a scheduled cue blocks deletion.
Select saved scenes, set optional per-step RGB channel, effect, brightness, effect speed, fade-in, fade-out, fade curve, and hold overrides (blank fields and Inherited scene values preserve the scene; 0 seconds inherits each scene's duration), choose Saved order or Stable daily shuffle, choose one or more targets, then save the playlist. Default and all-target modes are exclusive; selected mappings may optionally include the default bridge. Use Rename Playlist to migrate every scheduled-cue reference atomically before continuing to edit the renamed playlist.
Scheduled Scene Cues
Display a saved scene or a saved-scene playlist automatically at a chosen wall-clock time and time zone. Playlist cues use the saved order or stable daily shuffle for each repeat pass and keep each scene's RGB color, effect, and optional per-step brightness, duration, fade-in, fade-out, and fade-curve overrides (blank RGB/brightness/transitions and Inherited scene curves preserve the saved scene); their playback order, pass count, effective per-step RGB/brightness/durations/transitions/curves, start offsets, and total duration are shown in status, calendar, and history. Single-scene cues can override any saved-scene red, green, or blue channel from 0-255; blank channels inherit the saved scene, and effective RGB is included in status, occurrence exports, calendar metadata, and retained run history. The saved scene's effect and 25-400% animation speed are inherited by every single-scene cue. Leave the one-time date blank for a recurring cue, or set it to run exactly once; recurring cues can run daily, weekly on selected weekdays, monthly on a calendar day, monthly on an ordinal weekday such as the first Monday or last Friday, or yearly on a calendar date. Use the interval control for every-N-day/week/month/year cadences; intervals above 1 require a start date anchor. Optional inclusive end dates and exclusions still apply. Leave Hold duration blank (or enter 0) for the saved scene or playlist; a 1-30 second override is available only for single-scene cues because playlist steps have their own saved overrides. Set Maximum executions to 1-365 to stop a recurring cue after a finite number of attempts, or leave it at 0 for unlimited runs; the counter survives Jellyfin restarts and one-time cues still disable after their first successful run. Set Priority from 0-100 when several cues are due together; higher values run first and equal values keep saved order. Choose a playback policy per cue: Inherit global policy keeps the scheduler-wide setting, while Skip or Defer overrides it for this cue only. Saved-scene fade-in and fade-out transitions are inherited and clamped to fit the effective cue duration. Choose All enabled targets to run the cue sequentially on the default bridge and every distinct enabled user-mapped target, or multi-select a deliberate subset of enabled mappings and optionally the default bridge; each selected target is validated and reported without exposing credentials. Use Enable/Disable Cue to pause one rule without editing its schedule, Skip Next Cue to omit one upcoming automatic occurrence while keeping future recurrence, or Duplicate Cue to create a disabled copy with a fresh counter before making a variation. Cues are short, restorative previews: active playback wins, and the selected lights are always restored after the scene duration.
Select up to 50 cues, then run them sequentially with restorative cleanup, request cancellation, create disabled copies, enable or disable them, reset execution counters, mark/clear their next automatic occurrence, or delete them. Run Now preflights every reference and target before bridge activity, keeps per-cue failures, and stops remaining cues on cancellation.
Select scheduled cues to run them sequentially, request cancellation, duplicate disabled copies, or apply a bulk enabled-state, skipped-occurrence, counter-reset, or deletion action.
Use a fixed wall-clock time, solar noon, sunrise/sunset, civil dawn/dusk (6° below), nautical dawn/dusk (12° below), or astronomical dawn/dusk (18° below) from the cue's coordinates.
Offset is -720 to 720 minutes. Coordinates use decimal degrees: north/east are positive. Polar day/night dates without an event are skipped safely.
Blank or 0 uses the saved scene duration; 1-30 seconds overrides it for this cue. Playlist cues always use each scene's saved duration.
Blank channels inherit the saved scene's RGB values; explicit channels are bounded to 0-255. Playlist cues use their saved per-step colors.
Blank inherits the saved scene brightness; explicit values are bounded to 0-100%. Playlist cues use each step's saved brightness.
0 is unlimited; 1-365 stops after that many attempts.
0-100; higher-priority cues run first when due together. Equal priorities keep saved order.
Override the global playback policy for this cue only.
1 keeps the normal cadence. Higher values require Start date as the anchor.
Days beyond a month's length run on that month's final day.
Day 31 is clamped to the final day of the selected month.
Choose the first through fifth, or last, matching weekday in each month.
Choose one or more mappings or nested device routes for a selected-target cue. You may include the default bridge; All enabled targets is exclusive. Device routes carry only user and device IDs; credentials remain server-side.
Resolve duplicate user mappings before selecting affected scheduled-cue targets or all enabled targets.
Daily cues run on every calendar date; weekly cues choose one or more weekdays; monthly-day cues use the Day of month field; monthly-weekday cues use the ordinal weekday selector; yearly cues use the month and Day of month fields. The Every value multiplies the selected recurrence unit (days, weeks, months, or years); intervals above 1 use Start date as the stable anchor. Setting a one-time date disables recurring date rules and recurrence controls. The scheduler checks every few seconds and runs each cue at most once per selected-time-zone minute. Blank time zone keeps the server-local default. Dates are calendar dates in the selected cue time zone and include both endpoints. Enter excluded dates as comma-separated yyyy-MM-dd values to skip holidays or blackout days.
Cues contain only scene names, schedule timing/date rules, and target mapping/device-route IDs; bridge credentials remain server-side.
Pause automatic execution without deleting cues or changing their schedules. Upcoming previews and readiness remain available, and Run Now still runs an individual cue while automation is paused.
When greater than 0, a scheduler restart or short Jellyfin outage can recover the most recent automatic cue missed within this window. Older missed cues are not replayed in a burst; 0 keeps exact-minute behavior.
Playback always keeps control of the bridge. Skip preserves the immediate failure/attempt behavior; Defer holds one due occurrence and retries it after playback ends without consuming the cue's execution limit.
Any active playback preserves the historical process-wide behavior. Matching target rooms lets independent Hue areas run scheduled cues while another room is playing; cues with unresolved targets conservatively use the process-wide block.
When Defer is selected, the pending occurrence waits up to 1-120 minutes for playback to finish. If playback remains active, the occurrence is recorded as skipped; the next recurrence remains eligible.
Optional: store the bounded sanitized cue-run history in plugin configuration. Cue and target labels may be private metadata; disabling this setting removes stored history.
Keep 1-100 newest scheduled-cue runs in memory and, when retention is enabled, across restarts. The default is 100; reducing this trims older entries when you save.

Sync performance
Choose which Jellyfin video or audio item types can start Hue Sync. Audio uses a low/mid/high-band reactive visualizer. Changing this does not interrupt an active session; its normal progress and stop events still clean up safely.
Frames per second to analyze. Lower values reduce CPU load. (Default: 20)
Scales the low/mid/high audio-reactive loudness envelope when Audio or All media is selected (25-400%, default: 100%). This affects audio intensity without changing the final brightness boost.
Suppresses audio windows whose mixed RMS level is below this normalized threshold (0-100%, default: 0%). Zero preserves the original analyzer; higher values reduce low-level hiss and room noise.
Center frequency for the low/bass visualizer band (20-3900 Hz). It must remain below the mid and high centers; default: 90 Hz.
Center frequency for the midrange visualizer band (20-3900 Hz). It must remain between the low and high centers; default: 420 Hz.
Center frequency for the high/treble visualizer band (20-3900 Hz). It must remain above the low and mid centers; default: 1600 Hz.
Scales bass/low-band energy before palette rendering (0-200%, default: 100%). Zero mutes the band; values above 100% compensate for a weak low end.
Scales midrange energy before palette rendering (0-200%, default: 100%).
Scales treble/high-band energy before palette rendering (0-200%, default: 100%).
Blends each audio analysis window with the previous window (0-90%, default: 0%). Zero responds immediately; higher values reduce spectral flicker with a bounded release.
Averages each low/mid/high center across nearby frequencies by this percentage (0-100%, default: 0%). Zero preserves exact-center analysis; higher values catch content between centers.
Adds a transient brightness boost when audio energy rises (0-100%, default: 0%). Zero preserves the steady loudness response; higher values make beats and attacks flash more visibly.
Controls how much of an enabled beat pulse carries into the next frame (0-100%, default: 0%). Zero is an instant flash; higher values add a bounded, longer release tail.
Requires this minimum normalized rise before a beat pulse attacks (0-100%, default: 0%). Zero reacts to every upward change; higher values suppress small fluctuations.
Chooses how audio energy is rendered during Audio or All media playback. Spectrum preserves the original behavior; Band exposes low/mid/high energy as RGB, while Warm, Cool, and Monochrome provide room-friendly alternatives.
Chooses how low/mid/high audio energy is routed across the entertainment area's channels. Spatial preserves the original position-aware mapping; Uniform suits ambient whole-room playback; Mirror keeps matching left/right placements visually symmetric.
Mono averages the captured PCM channels before analysis. Stereo preserves left/right energy and blends it across physical channel positions when Spatial routing is selected. Left or Right uses only that source channel for Spatial routing; Uniform and Mirror remain intentionally symmetric.
Choose the RGB frame size sent through the sampler. Higher resolution preserves finer spatial detail but uses more CPU and memory.
Stretch fills the 16:9 sampler exactly. Fit preserves the source aspect ratio with bars; Crop preserves it while trimming the excess edges.
Use Auto for television or DVD sources that carry interlaced frame flags. On forces deinterlacing for every frame and uses more CPU.
Size of the neighborhood sampled around each Hue channel's screen position (1-50%, default: 15%). Smaller values follow fine detail; larger values reduce noise.
Choose how each Hue channel's sampling region is combined. Average is the stable default; center-weighted favors detail near the mapped position; center pixel follows the exact position.
Corrects a physically mirrored, flipped, or rotated entertainment area. The selected orientation applies to video sampling and audio spatial routing; Normal preserves the bridge layout.
Blend the previous frame into new colors to reduce flicker (0-90%, default: 0). Higher values create smoother but slower transitions.
Adds -hwaccel auto to ffmpeg to lighten CPU use when available.
Optional decoder, thread, and hardware flags (for example -hwaccel vaapi -threads 2 or -c:v h264_cuvid). Extra inputs, outputs, protocols, headers, filters, scripts, and paths are rejected.
Stop sync and restore the lights when FFmpeg produces no complete frame for this long (1-60 seconds, default: 5). Initial codec startup receives a longer grace period.
Cinema Mode
Automatically dim lights when playback starts.
Brightness level for cinema mode dimming (0-100%).
Playback Pause Behavior
Choose whether pausing playback leaves the last Hue colors in place, restores the lights captured when playback started, or dims each captured light to the configured cinema level. Sync resumes automatically when playback continues.
Per-User Bridge Mappings
Map individual Jellyfin users to specific Hue bridges and entertainment areas. Users without a mapping will use the default bridge settings above. To keep a per-user profile while using that same bridge, leave every bridge target field blank. Use View References before disabling or deleting a mapping that scheduled cues or saved playlists may use.
Select user mappings to enable, disable, or delete them together. Scheduled-cue references block disabling and deletion; disabling also clears stored custom bridge targets.
Reconciliation checks persisted mapping IDs and names against Jellyfin users without reading or exposing Hue credentials.
Add New User Mapping

Per-user Performance Profile (optional)
Leave any field blank to inherit the global capture and sampling setting. These controls let a mapped user trade CPU usage for spatial detail without changing other users.
Optional per-user analysis rate (1-60 FPS).

Leave blank to inherit the global bridge address, credentials, entertainment area, and channel profile. For a custom bridge, enter all bridge fields.

Stored securely on the server. Leave blank to keep the stored key; use Link Bridge or enter a replacement manually. Test Connection verifies the DTLS stream when available.
Paste the entertainment area UUID here.

Each route needs its own private bridge address, App Key, Client Key, and entertainment area. Advanced Settings
Save and restore the original light state before/after sync.
Brightness multiplier for synced colors (50-200%, default: 100).
White Balance / RGB Channel Gains
Adjust individual RGB channels to correct a room's color bias. 100% is neutral; gains apply before saturation and hue shift.
Red channel multiplier (50-200%, default: 100).
Green channel multiplier (50-200%, default: 100).
Blue channel multiplier (50-200%, default: 100).
Color saturation adjustment (0-200%, default: 100).
Rotate synced colors around the hue wheel (-180 to 180 degrees, default: 0). Use this to correct a room's color bias or apply a creative palette.
Final brightness scale applied to synced colors after boost, gains, temperature, gamma, contrast, saturation, and hue shift (0-100%, default: 100). Use this to cap the room brightness without changing color balance.
Adjust mid-tone brightness after gains (0.5-2.5, default: 1.0). Values above 1.0 lift mid-tones; values below 1.0 deepen them.
Expand or compress contrast around mid-gray after gamma (50-200%, default: 100%). Higher values deepen shadows and brighten highlights.
Warm or cool synced colors from 1000-20000 K after channel gains (default: 6500 K neutral daylight). Lower values warm the room; higher values cool it.
Set lights to black when average brightness is below this value (0-255, default: 15).
When a sampled frame is below the blackout threshold, either send black to the room or preserve the last streamed colors (default: Blackout).
Minimum color change to trigger update (0-255, 0=disabled, default: 10).
Number of retry attempts for Hue REST requests and DTLS stream recovery (0-10, default: 3). Set to 0 to disable reconnect attempts.
If enabled, lights will react to supported video and audio playback in real-time (uses CPU/GPU resources).
